title: Minimum Score After Removals on a Tree
summary: Given an undirected connected tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and a value array for each node, remove two distinct edges to form three connected components.
statement: Given an undirected connected tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and a value array for each node, remove two distinct edges to form three connected components. For each component, compute the XOR of the node values. Determine the difference between the largest and smallest XOR values for the three components. Return the minimum score achievable by any pair of edge removals.
constraints: nums has 3 through 1000 values and edges form a zero-indexed tree.
Remove two distinct edges; XOR node values within each of the resulting three components.
Minimize maximum component XOR minus minimum component XOR.
hints: Root the tree and compute every subtree XOR plus ancestor intervals.
Each removed edge corresponds to the child-side subtree below it.
For two cut nodes, use ancestor intervals to distinguish nested subtrees from disjoint subtrees and derive the three XORs.
Subtree XOR cancellation gives each component exactly; enumerating all cut-node pairs covers every pair of removed edges.
editorial: Subtree XOR cancellation gives each component exactly; enumerating all cut-node pairs covers every pair of removed edges.

tests.explanation: The best pair of cuts produces component XOR values whose range is nine.
Choosing the optimal two edges makes all three component XOR values equal, so the score is zero.
